name: Irredentism
summary: Irredentism is the policy of a state, usually together with kin living across the border, of retrieving territory and co-ethnic people held by a neighbouring state, so that a nation and its ancestral homeland sit in one state it controls. The word comes from the Italian Italia irredenta movement of the 1870s. Scholars treat it as a sub-type of nationalism and distinguish it from simple expansion, diasporic politics and secession; it has no programme or canonical text of its own.
scope: The family-like principle as defined by comparative scholarship (Fuzesi 2006; Malbasic and Trbojevic 2020; the Encyclopedia of Political Science entry). Member movements (Greater Serbia, Greater Albania, Megali Idea, Pan-Germanism, Hungarian revisionism) are not used as evidence and answer under their own entries. Most statements are null because the definitions say nothing on them.
